items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: I remember he talked about Santo Giuffre. He told me that Santo Giuffre had made, had refaced a mouthpiece for him... Santo Giuffre used to play in the Tulane Theater with my, when my dad played there... In fact, Santo Giuffre is the man that learned my mother how to cook, uh, Italian dishes.

ctx.x: Conquer Johnny Lawler used to play with him. Who? Johnny Lawler used to play with him in Chicago, I think, Conquer Johnson. Well, you know, Johnny Lawler told me about him years ago.

Yeah, well, anyway, I think he was playing piano. But they had, well, I tell you, the guy on that saxophone was terrific. Man, that guy could play some saxophone. He played more like, yeah, that's the fella, that's the one band, they were over there when Barney and I went over and played with Charlie because they had some kind of a difference. And we stood over, we stood over, Dan and I, I don't know, where was playing carnet. Well, anyway, Dan and I stood over that night. We had heard somebody had said how good…
I think between, uh, Berks and Palmyra. Now, the Six and Magazine bunch, that was the Cassards from up there.
